The contract compiles cleanly (compiler 0.36.0) after four fixes in `contract/token.compact`. I only compiled it and didn't run any tests.

1. **`totalSupply` wasn't readable.** It was a plain `ledger` field, so apps couldn't read it. I changed it to `export ledger totalSupply`.
2. **`mint` didn't compile.** `balanceAt(recipient) + value` produces a wider integer type than the `Uint<64>` the map stores. I added `as Uint<64>`, which also makes it fail on overflow instead of wrapping.
3. **`transfer` had the same cast problem.** I added `as Uint<64>` to its recipient credit.
4. **`transfer` used `from` as a variable name.** `from` is a reserved word in Compact, so I renamed it to `sender`.

I left the interface, the `burn` logic and the supply accounting alone. `transfer` moves balance between accounts without touching `totalSupply`, so the supply still equals the sum of balances.

The contract compiles cleanly (compiler 0.36.0) after four fixes in `contract/token.compact`. I only compiled it and didn't run any tests.

1. **`totalSupply` wasn't readable.** It was a plain `ledger` field, so apps couldn't read it. I changed it to `export ledger totalSupply`.
2. **`mint` didn't compile.** `balanceAt(recipient) + value` produces a wider integer type than the `Uint<64>` the map stores. I added `as Uint<64>`, which also makes it fail on overflow instead of wrapping.
3. **`transfer` had the same cast problem.** I added `as Uint<64>` to its recipient credit.
4. **`transfer` used `from` as a variable name.** `from` is a reserved word in Compact, so I renamed it to `sender`.

I left the interface, the `burn` logic and the supply accounting alone. `transfer` moves balance between accounts without touching `totalSupply`, so the supply still equals the sum of balances.
